You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
1. The test "testArDelete" tries to create an ar archive with two files: "test1.xml" and "test2.xml".
2. Then it attempts to delete "test2.xml" by reading the original archive (bla.ar) and copying only the entries that are not "test2.xml" into a new archive (bla2.ar).
3. During the copying, it reads entries with ArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry(), which internally calls ArArchiveInputStream.getNextArEntry().
4. In the method ArArchiveInputStream.getNextArEntry(), the header is read, and then the entry fields including name and length are parsed. If the offset is 0, the global header "<arch>" is expected and consumed.
5. The test report indicates that the deletion is not effective: although getNextEntry() returns only "test1.xml" (indicating "test2.xml" is deleted), the resulting archive still contains both "test1.xml" and "test2.xml" when checked with the system "ar" program.
6. This suggests that the archive data of the deleted entry "test2.xml" was still present in the output archive.
7. Looking closely at the test code, when an entry is to be deleted, the test copies the entry data to a ByteArrayOutputStream but does not properly skip over the entry data or manage the offsets.
8. Investigating the ArArchiveInputStream.getNextArEntry() method shows that it only reads the header and metadata of an entry, but does not skip the data content of the entry after it is processed.
9. Thus, when the test tries to copy or skip entries, the position in the input stream might not be correctly aligned for the next entry, potentially causing the copying of data of "deleted" entries inadvertently.
10. The recent bug report mentioning "getNextEntry() method doesn't skip over datafields correctly" is relevant here: it indicates a problem with the skipping of entry data when iterating entries.
11. If ArArchiveInputStream.getNextArEntry() does not internally handle skipping the data content of the previous entry, the archive input stream will be misaligned on the next read, causing incorrect reading/copying of entries.
12. Consequently, the "deletion" by not copying the entry data is ineffective because the underlying stream position is not correctly managed, leading to residual data of deleted files in the resulting archive.

Hence, the root cause is that ArArchiveInputStream.getNextArEntry() (and potentially related read/skip logic) does not correctly skip the entry data after processing the header, leading to erroneous archive output when deleting entries by copying. The test's deletion logic exposes this bug because it relies on properly positioned input streams to exclude certain entries.

This explains why the command-line "ar -t" still shows "test2.xml" in the supposedly updated archive, although getNextEntry() doesn't return it: the underlying archive content was not adjusted correctly due to improper skipping.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
